newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Finance Ministry issues T-Bill calendar.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Finance Ministry issues T-Bill calendar.

text.p: The Dutch Ministry of Finance said on Friday its Agency would standardize its Dutch Treasury Certificate (DTC) programmes from July 1, to boost the transparency concerning planned DTC issues.

"DTCs must be available in a range of remaining maturities. By increasing the transparency of the DTC issuance policy, market participants are in a position to timely take advantage of available maturities as well," the Agency said.
Dutch Treasury Certificates are short-term state paper, issued at a discount to face value.
From now on, only DTCs with an initial maturity of three and 12 months will be issued, the Agency said, while a calendar of DTC-programmes would be announced in due time prior to subscription.
"Every month, an existing programme will be redeemed and a new programme opened for subscription," the Agency said.

Such programmes will generally have a standard maturity of three months. However, when the oldest 12-month programme has just three months left to run, a new 12-month programme will be opened, it said.
As a one-off transitional measure, two programmes are to be opened in July, the Agency said.
Each programme may raise a maximum 7.5 billion guilders, while the total to be raised by DTCs in issue is subject to a ceiling of 30 billion guilders, the Agency said.
Since January 1997, the Government has stabilized its balance with the Nederlandsche Bank at a level of 50 million guilders, using Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) as a prime instrument.
The Finance Ministry's Agency said the amount outstanding in DTCs currently totalled 27.392 million guilders in four programmes.
These programmes respectively mature today, on June 30, July 31 and December 31.
Two days ago, the ministry opened a new DTC programme with a maximum issue amount of 7.5 billion guilders.
The programme, which matures on August 28, is currently priced at 3.12 percent.
The Agency said the calendar of DTC issues for the 12 months starting July would be as follows:
July 1997 3-month DTC + 12-month DTC
August 1997 3-month DTC
September 1997 3-month DTC
October 1997 12-month DTC
November 1997 3-month DTC
December 1997 3-month DTC
January 1998 3-month DTC
February 1998 3-month DTC
March 1998 3-month DTC
April 1998 12-month DTC
May 1998 3-month DTC
June 1998 3-month DTC.
